chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who has two varieties of one type of food, and their price is one thing, and one of the two is better than the other. So he mixes them both together, then he sells them both for one price. He said: 'It is not correct for him to do that; he is cheating the Muslims by it, until he clarifies it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling mixed food items of different qualities at a single price?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that mixing superior and inferior goods of the same type and selling them as a uniform lot without disclosure constitutes 'ghish' (deception), a key concept in Shia commercial jurisprudence. This ruling emphasizes the seller's duty of transparency to ensure fair value exchange, reflecting the broader ethical imperative of avoiding hidden defects in trade. The hadith underscores that mere physical mixture does not justify uniform pricing if the quality disparity is not explicitly communicated to the buyer.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happened to have two varieties of one foodstuff with him, and both their prices are of one price, and one of the two is better than the other. So he mixes them both together, then he sells both for the one price. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not correct for him that he does that. He is cheating the Muslims by it, until he clarifies it (to the buyers)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a man who has various kinds of the same item of foodstuff of the same price of which one is of high quality and one is of low quality but he mixes them together; then sells them for one kind of price. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not proper for him and it is cheating the Muslims unless he informs them of the condition.’”
